items.question: Under what certification basis is the H145 D3 (BK117 D-3) certified, per Sect. 2.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.3 states the helicopter is certified under CS/FAR 29 requirements.

items.question: Under what conditions may the H145 D3 be flown by a single pilot from the LEFT crew seat, per Sect. 2.4?
options: VFR only, no passenger in the right seat, rotor brake not required for the mission, and a normal (not short) collective lever installed
VFR or IFR, as long as autopilot is engaged
Never permitted from the left seat under any conditions
Only during training flights with an instructor in the right seat
items.explanation: Sect. 2.4: single-pilot operation from the left seat requires VFR flight, no passenger in the right seat, rotor brake not required, and a normal collective lever (not the short collective) installed.

items.question: What is the maximum number of occupants (including flight crew) approved for the H145 D3, per Sect. 2.4?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.4 states the maximum number of occupants is 10 persons, including the flight crew.

items.question: Which environmental conditions are explicitly prohibited per Sect. 2.5.2, in addition to known icing?
options: Flight in volcanic ash, and (if IRS is installed) flight in a salty environment
Flight above 15,000 ft PA in any conditions
Flight in rain of any intensity
Flight over water beyond 25 NM from shore
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.2: flight into known icing, flight in volcanic ash, and (if IRS is installed) flight in a salty environment are all prohibited.

items.question: What is the maximum wind speed for starting and stopping the rotor, per Sect. 2.5.3?
options: 40 kt from the front or rear only
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.3: starting and stopping the rotor is authorized with wind from any horizontal direction up to 50 kt.

items.question: Per the slope landing limits in Sect. 2.5.5, what is the maximum slope for ground sloping up to the LEFT?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.5 lists max slope of 8° for ground sloping up to the left, 12° sloping up to the right, 10° nose down (if tail clearance allows), and 8° nose up.

items.question: In case of mast moment indication failure, what is the maximum slope limit per Sect. 2.5.5?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.5.5 note: in case of mast moment indication failure, the maximum slope limit is 3°.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.6.2, below what height AGL must the aircraft be flown manually at all times (any AFCS mode)?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.2: below 10 ft AGL, the aircraft shall be flown manually, regardless of AFCS mode.

items.question: Activation of the Go-Around (GA) mode is prohibited below what height AGL, per Sect. 2.6.2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.2: activation of the Go-Around (GA) mode below 4 ft AGL is prohibited.

items.question: What is the minimum airspeed under Instrument Flight (V-MINI) with the 4-axis AFCS ON (three upper modes engaged), per Sect. 2.6.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.3: with 4-axis AFCS ON (three upper modes engaged), V-MINI is 30 KIAS; with two or fewer upper modes engaged it is 60 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum glideslope angle approved for an LPV or LNAV/VNAV approach, per Sect. 2.6.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.3: maximum glideslope angle is 6.7° for ILS approaches and 10.0° for LPV and LNAV/VNAV approaches.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.6.4, training in Instrument Flight conditions using DSAS mode (A.TRIM OFF) requires what minimum crew?
options: One pilot plus an instructor observer on the ground
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.4: for training in Instrument Flight conditions in DSAS mode, a minimum crew of two pilots is required, and the aircraft shall be flown manually.

items.question: In backup SAS or AFCS OFF mode, what is the maximum bank angle permitted, per Sect. 2.6.4?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.4: in backup SAS or AFCS OFF mode the aircraft shall be flown manually, at a maximum bank angle of 45° and maximum airspeed of 110 KIAS or VNE, whichever is less.

items.question: Which GTN main software version must be installed on a GTN750Xi unit for approved IFR navigation, per Sect. 2.7.2?
options: Any version, no restriction applies to the Xi unit
items.explanation: Sect. 2.7.2: GTN750 units require MAIN SW version 6.62; GTN750Xi units require MAIN SW version 20.12 or 20.30. Use of subsequent software versions requires prior airworthiness approval.

items.question: Why is use of USER MAGNETIC VARIATION on the GTN prohibited, per Sect. 2.7.2?
options: Helionix does not support a user (manual) magnetic variation, which could cause erroneous indications and erratic autopilot behavior
It disables the HTAWS function permanently
It is only prohibited during IFR flight, not VFR
It voids the aircraft's transponder calibration
items.explanation: Sect. 2.7.2: because Helionix does not support a user (manual) magnetic variation, erroneous indications and erratic autopilot behavior could result when user magnetic variation is selected.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.7.3, what is prohibited regarding the Synthetic Vision System (SVS)?
options: Simultaneous display of SVS on all MFDs
Using SVS during an ILS approach
items.explanation: Sect. 2.7.3: simultaneous display of SVS on all MFDs is prohibited.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.7.7, if the optional Inertial Reference System (IRS) is installed and replaces AHRS3, what is explicitly prohibited?
options: Using the OFF or NAV position of the IRS switch, and using the IRS lat/long position or control functions on the GTN 750Xi HNS pages
Using the IRS at all during IFR flight
Installing IRS on any BK117 D-3 aircraft
items.explanation: Sect. 2.7.7: if IRS is installed and replaces AHRS3, it is prohibited to use the OFF or NAV position of the IRS switch, to use the lat/long IRS position on the GTN 750Xi HNS status pages for navigation, or to use the IRS control functions on the GTN 750Xi HNS pages.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.8.1, what is the maximum approved gross mass for flight of the H145 D3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.8.1: maximum approved gross mass for flight is 3800 kg (100 kg more than the H145 D2's 3700 kg).

items.question: What is the minimum approved gross mass for flight of the H145 D3, per Sect. 2.8.2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.8.2: minimum approved gross mass for flight is 2000 kg.

items.question: What is the maximum allowable load per cabin tie-down ring, per Sect. 2.8.4?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.8.4: maximum allowable load per tie-down ring is 70 kg.

items.question: On the airspeed indicator, what does the dashed red/yellow line represent, per Sect. 2.10.1?
options: V NE power off – maximum speed in autorotation / power off conditions
V NE – maximum speed in AEO or OEI
Maximum tailwind component for steep approaches
items.explanation: Sect. 2.10.1: the solid red line is V NE (max speed AEO/OEI), while the dashed red/yellow line is V NE power off (max speed in autorotation/power-off conditions).

items.question: What is the maximum V NE in AEO, per Sect. 2.10.1?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.10.1: the maximum V NE in AEO is 150 KIAS. VNE in OEI is the lesser of 110 KIAS and VNE in AEO; VNE power off is the lesser of 90 KIAS and VNE in AEO.

items.question: What is the maximum operating altitude for hover in ground effect, takeoff and landing, per Sect. 2.11.1?
options: 20000 ft PA or DA, whichever is less
15000 ft PA or DA, whichever is less
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.1: maximum operating altitude for hover in ground effect / takeoff and landing is 20000 ft PA or DA, whichever is less.

items.question: In the basic aircraft configuration, what is the minimum ambient air temperature limit, per Sect. 2.11.2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.2: basic aircraft configuration minimum air temperature is -30°C. With oil cooler blocking plates installed (cold weather kit), the minimum is -45°C.

items.question: If OAT is 40°C or above, what is the maximum operating time on ground, per Sect. 2.11.2?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.2: if OAT ≥ +40°C, the maximum operating time on ground is limited to 30 minutes.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.12, at what gross mass threshold does the minimum continuous NR value increase from 80% to 85%?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.12: minimum continuous NR is 85% for gross mass above 2250 kg, and 80% for gross mass below 2250 kg (the H145 D2 uses a 2200 kg threshold instead).

items.question: Up to what NR value is rotor brake operation permitted, per Sect. 2.12?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.12: rotor brake use is permitted from 0 to 50% NR.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.13.2, what is the AEO max continuous torque limit per engine, and above what airspeed does the amber torque range begin to gradually disappear?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.2: AEO max continuous torque is 2×74%; the amber torque range gradually disappears between VY+10kt and VY+25kt (the H145 D2 uses VY+5kt to VY+20kt instead).

items.question: Per Sect. 2.13.2, what is the OEI 30-second power torque limit?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.2 OEI torque limitations: max continuous 100%, 2-minute power 143%, 30-second power 150%.

items.question: During engine start, what is the continuous starting TOT limit, per Sect. 2.13.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.3: continuous starting TOT limit is 760°C; the starting transient limit is 840°C for max 10 seconds, after which an automatic stop function interrupts the start.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.14.2, is simultaneous use of FADEC EMER mode on both engines permitted?
options: No, usage of FADEC EMER mode on both engines simultaneously is not permitted
Yes, but only above 10000 ft PA
Yes, but only during training flights
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.2: usage of FADEC EMER mode on both engines simultaneously is not permitted. It is also not permitted during engine start, in training mode, or in OEI (except per specific MEL/MMEL provisions).

items.question: What is the maximum uninterrupted operating time of the engines (FLIGHT or IDLE), per Sect. 2.14.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.3: maximum uninterrupted operating time of the engines (FLIGHT or IDLE) is 12 hours.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.14.4, after 3 starting/ventilation attempts, what waiting period must be observed before further attempts?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.4: a 60-second wait is required between starting/ventilation attempts; after 3 attempts, a 30-minute waiting period shall be observed. Ventilating both engines simultaneously is prohibited.

items.question: What is the total maximum continuous electrical load from both generators operative, per Sect. 2.14.5?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.5: maximum continuous load per generator is 200 A below 15000 ft (180 A above), with a total maximum continuous load of 360 A from both generators operative.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.14.6, during sideward flight or sideways slope landing, a low MGB oil pressure indication in one system is acceptable for how long, provided the other system is normal?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.6 note: this condition is acceptable for up to 7 minutes consecutively; the pilot is alerted by MGB TREND after 5 minutes and MGB OVERLIMIT caution after 7 minutes.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.15.1, at what mast moment level does the amber caution range begin?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.15.1: mast moment below 54% requires no alert; 54–68% shows the amber caution indication; above 68% triggers the red indication plus a repeating 'Mast Moment' voice message (the H145 D2 uses a lower 66% red threshold instead of 68%).

items.question: Per Sect. 2.15.2, for nose-up slope operations at high gross mass (≥3500 kg) in hot-and-high conditions, how far can the mast moment limitation be additionally reduced?
options: Down to 41% (depending on weight, altitude and temperature)
Down to 20% fixed, regardless of conditions
It is not reduced further under any condition
Down to 54%, matching the normal amber threshold
items.explanation: Sect. 2.15.2: for nose-up slope limitations at high gross mass (≥3500 kg) in hot and high conditions, an additional reduction of the mast moment limitation down to 41% (depending on weight, altitude and temperature) applies.

items.question: What is the maximum fuel viscosity permitted at all temperatures, per Sect. 2.16?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.16: maximum fuel viscosity (all temperatures) is 12 cSt.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.16.3, what is the maximum allowed concentration (curative treatment) of the Biobor JF fuel biocide?
options: 0.1 ml per liter of fuel (curative) / 0.2 ml per liter (preventive/shock)
1.0 ml per liter for both curative and preventive treatment
0.01 ml per liter, far lower than for preventive treatment
Biocides are not approved for use on the BK117 D-3
items.explanation: Sect. 2.16.3: Biobor JF is the approved fuel biocide, with a curative treatment concentration of 0.1 ml/liter and a preventive (shock) treatment concentration of 0.2 ml/liter. Wrong dosing can damage fuel system or engine components.

items.question: What is the total usable fuel quantity for the H145 D3, per Sect. 2.16.4?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.16.4: total usable fuel is 903.8 litres / 723.0 kg (main tank + LH/RH supply tanks combined), the same fuel system capacity as the H145 D2.

items.question: What is the maximum oil temperature (high red limit) for the engine oil, per Sect. 2.17.1?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.17.1: maximum engine oil temperature (high red limit) is 117°C.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.18, what action involving the HYD TEST switch is prohibited during flight?
options: Operating the HYD TEST switch during flight is not permitted
Only the LH hydraulic system may be tested in flight
HYD TEST may be used only above 500 ft AGL
HYD TEST is required before every landing
items.explanation: Sect. 2.18: the HYD TEST switch must not be operated during flight.

items.question: What is the maximum hydraulic pressure before the high-pressure relief valve fully opens with max fluid flow, per Sect. 2.18.1?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.18.1: continuous operation range is 90–120 bar; the relief valve begins to open at 120–122 bar, and maximum pressure with the relief valve open and max fluid flow is 150 bar.

items.question: What hydraulic fluid type is authorized for use at all ambient temperatures, per Sect. 2.18.3?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.18.3: hydraulic fluid type MIL-H-5606 is authorized for use at all ambient temperatures.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.19, what mass value is shown on the placard located below the forward RH cabin door?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.19: the placard 'MAX. PERMISS. GROSS MASS 3800kg' is located below the forward RH cabin door, matching the Sect. 2.8.1 limit (the H145 D2's equivalent placard reads 3700kg).

items.question: Per Sect. 2.14.4, what is the maximum ventilation time for the engine starter when powered by the EPU?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.14.4: maximum ventilation time is 20 seconds with battery power, or 15 seconds with EPU power.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.8.5, what is the maximum load rating of the forward and middle multi-purpose cabin brackets for securing equipment (not persons)?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.8.5: the forward and middle multi-purpose brackets sustain a max load of 8000N — up to 200 kg per bracket for securing persons, or up to 40 kg per bracket for securing equipment. The aft brackets are limited to 10 kg of equipment.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.6.2, what is the operating rule for the CRHT autopilot mode?
options: Use is limited to flight over water or over flat and obstacle-free surfaces
CRHT may be used over any terrain provided AP2 is engaged
CRHT is only usable in IMC conditions
CRHT is prohibited entirely on the H145 D3
items.explanation: Sect. 2.6.2: use of the CRHT mode is limited to flight over water or over flat and obstacle-free surfaces.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.11.2, with the oil cooler blocking plates (cold weather kit) installed, what is the minimum ambient air temperature?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.11.2: with oil cooler blocking plates installed, minimum air temperature is -45°C (maximum remains +35°C); without the cold weather kit, minimum is -30°C.

items.question: Per Sect. 2.13.1, unintended power applications up to the FLI red teardrop transient limit are permitted for a maximum duration of how long?
items.explanation: Sect. 2.13.1: unintended power applications up to the transient limit (red teardrop) are permitted for a maximum duration of 12 seconds; each exceedance requires maintenance action and logbook entry.
